researcher_notes: IDENTIFIED THE PROJECT: GEM's ammonia unit traces (via the gem.wiki record's sole citation, h2inframap.eu, read for leads only) to the GIE/ENTSOG Hydrogen Infrastructure Map entry 'Dunkerque New Molecules development' (promoter Dunkerque LNG, carrier ammonia, open-access NH3 import terminal with cracking, PCI-flagged) = EU PCI no. 9.13 'Ammonia reception facility Dunkerque (FR)' (promoter Dunkerque LNG; 1-2 deep-sea jetties, up to 3x100,000 m3 NH3 tanks, up to 3 NH3-to-H2 cracking units, connection to the FR-BE open-access H2 backbone; commissioning 2035 per the Dec-2025 CINEA fiche PCIFiche_9.13_1st_PCI_PMI_list.pdf). Year 2023 = the year the project first appears publicly: selected on the EU's first PCI/PMI list under revised TEN-E, adopted by the European Commission 28 Nov 2023 (Annex to C(2023) 7930, ref 1, primary/regulatory: '9.13 Ammonia reception facility Dunkerque (FR)'). Independent French press (Banque des Territoires/Localtis, ref 2) covered the 2023 list naming 'des installations de reception d'ammoniac a Dunkerque' among the French PCIs. Consistent with Dunkerque LNG's 2023 'new molecules (CO2, hydrogen, ammonia)' strategy statements (Apr 2023 newsletter, found by prior pass). No pre-2023 public trace found (PCI candidacy was submitted non-publicly in 2022; FR+EN searches found no 2022 announcement; the Fluxys/Advario 2022 ammonia terminal is Antwerp, a different project). Caveat: 2023 anchors the first public proposal via the PCI listing rather than a promoter open-season/FEED press release - none exists to date.

No dated construction-start event exists; the 'construction' status itself is uncorroborated. TRACED GEM'S SOURCE: the gem.wiki record cites the IGU World LNG Report 2025 (ref [4]) for Expansion 2's construction status; that is Appendix 6 'Table of LNG Receiving Terminals Under Construction, end-2024', row 243: 'France, Fos Cavaou 2, [start year] 2026, 2.00 MTPA, ENGIE (100%), Onshore' (live copy: https://www.datocms-assets.com/146580/1751026179-igu-world-lng-report-2025-hr_dp_c.pdf; the ...1749457104... URL GEM cited is now 404). That row asserts a STATUS at a snapshot date (end-2024), not a dated works kickoff, and it is contradicted everywhere else: (a) no Elengy/Fosmax press release, CRE deliberation, EPC award, or French trade press reports any groundbreaking/site works for a second expansion (searched FR+EN incl. CRE deliberations/legifrance); (b) Elengy's program delivered the +2.5 bcm/y sold for Jan 2025-2040 via technical debottlenecking completed 2022-2023 (GIIGNL 2025 lists 'Fos Cavaou Expansion', 1.2 MTPA, start year 2022, alongside the 6.8 MTPA base; GIIGNL 2023: capacity to 8 MTPA in May 2023) - that is GEM's Expansion 1, operating 2023; (c) the further extension (up to 4.5 bcm/y offered from April 2030, Open Season 2021) has no reported FID; (d) GIIGNL 2026 (May 2026, repo archive) lists Fos Cavaou at 8.0 MTPA with NO expansion under construction, and its France section reports only bio-LNG services. Staging 2024 off the IGU snapshot would force a weak year for the wrong milestone (under-construction-at-date != construction start) against contradicting sources -> UNRESOLVED. RECOMMEND DATA FIX: re-verify the status 'construction/actual' itself; a single IGU appendix row against Elengy/CRE/GIIGNL silence suggests the unit is still pre-FID proposed, not under construction.

THIRD PASS - CONFIRMED NO RETIREMENT YEAR EXISTS AND NONE CAN: the Puerto Brisa (Terminal Brisa, Dibulla/La Guajira) LNG import-regasification terminal has never been built or operated. It remains a LIVE, forward-looking project: developer Energy Developments LLC + TransEnergy LNG (Kogas-Tech engineering) targets first operations of the initial stage (BALA-type tanks, 30,000 m3, 180-240 MPCD expandable to 400 MPCD) around end-2026, and Colombian press through 2024-2026 consistently uses the future tense ('construiran'). Regulator sweep found no datable retirement/cancellation event: ANLA's 2025-2026 regasification resolutions for La Guajira/Caribbean (Chuchupa-Ballena, Puerto El Cayao expansion, Cienaga LNG, Rio Cordoba, etc.) contain no Puerto Brisa LNG licence revocation or archiving; UPME/CREG materials list no retirement. The status 'retired' + substatus 'planned' = at best a PLANNED future retirement placeholder (perhaps for the interim Phase-1 tank configuration being superseded by a later phase), i.e. a not-yet-occurred milestone with no real-world date - same structural class as the FID+planned bucket. The verifications carried here support the anomaly finding (project live/never operated), not a year. RECOMMEND DATA FIX, NOT A YEAR: flag st_id 3806 to the data team - a never-operated terminal cannot have an actual retirement; the timeline row should be re-statused (or the year deliberately left blank as a future placeholder).

THIRD PASS - STILL ONLY A PLAN, NO DATED EVENT: the BW Batangas FSRU (First Gen interim offshore LNG terminal, Batangas) remains in service and neither First Gen/FGEN LNG, BW LNG, nor the Philippine DOE has announced any dated decommissioning/demobilization decision. Facts as of mid-2026: FSRU arrived Jun 2023, commissioned Sep-Oct 2023; FGEN LNG holds a 25-year permit to operate (Jan 2025); the BW time-charter is 5 years (nominally to ~2028, extendable - BW describes the deployment as up to ten years); Jun 2025 Prime Infrastructure Capital agreed to take 60% of FGEN LNG (First Gen and Tokyo Gas 20% each) with no announced change to the interim-FSRU plan; the replacement onshore FGEN Batangas LNG Terminal has no announced construction schedule or completion date. The 'retirement' exists only as the design intent that the interim FSRU is retired once the permanent onshore terminal is built - a future milestone with no defensible year. RECOMMEND DATA FIX: flag the status=retired + substatus=planned pattern (same structural class as the FID+planned bucket, and same class as Puerto Brisa st_id 3806) to the data team; these rows are future placeholders that should not be counted as missing-year gaps.
